title: Last Day to Mail a Letter or Card in Canada for the Holidays (2026)
abstract: Canada Post's send-by dates for cards and letters within Canada are December 22 for local mail, December 21 for regional mail and December 18 for national mail. Mail to the United States should go by December 11, and overseas cards by December 9 to 11 depending on the country. Lettermail has delivery standards of two, three and four business days that are estimates, not guarantees, so post early. If you are ordering a printed letter online, allow one business day for printing and posting before the Canada Post deadline. Santa Claus letters go to H0H 0H0 and need no stamp.

title: Canada Post's $2 Stamp in 2027: What Is Known and What Is Not
abstract: Budget 2026 says the price of a single domestic stamp will rise from $1.44 to $2.00 in 2027, then rise about seven per cent a year. No month has been announced and Canada Post has not published a new rate table. The booklet, coil and pane price of $1.24 and the U.S. and international rates have not been confirmed. A Permanent stamp is always accepted at the current domestic rate, so one bought now stays valid after an increase. This page shows the official rates today, the proposal, and what to check on Canada Post's price pages.

title: Can You Track a Letter in Canada?
abstract: Standard Lettermail has no tracking number, so an ordinary letter cannot be tracked. The one tracked option for a letter is Registered Mail, which costs $13.15 plus the letter's postage and includes a signature, proof of mailing and delivery confirmation. Parcels and packets can be tracked, but a letter in an envelope is Lettermail. This guide explains what each option gives you, what it costs, and when an ordinary letter is enough.

title: My Letter Has Not Arrived: What to Do in Canada
abstract: Canada Post's standard for Lettermail is two business days locally, three in a province and four across Canada, not guaranteed. Its help page says most delayed letters arrive within five business days of the usual standard, and that individual letters without tracking numbers cannot be investigated. After that you can send feedback through a support ticket, though it will not receive a direct response. Check the address and postal code, confirm the postage, and ask the recipient to check neighbours and the community mailbox.

title: How to Prove You Mailed a Letter in Canada
abstract: Ordinary mail gives no proof that a letter was sent or received. Registered Mail gives a date-stamped receipt from the post office, a signature on delivery and delivery confirmation. For a notice that must be provable, check whether the contract or the rule requires a particular method, keep a copy of exactly what you sent, and note the date. This guide compares the ways to keep proof, what each costs, and what an online mailing service can and cannot give you.

title: How to Mail a Letter in Canada: A First-Time Guide
abstract: To mail a standard letter in Canada, put it in an envelope, write the recipient's address in the centre and your return address in the top left corner, add a stamp, and post it in a mailbox or at a post office. A standard letter up to 30 grams needs one Permanent stamp, worth $1.24. Include the full six-character postal code, because a missing code is charged at higher rates. This guide is for newcomers and anyone who has never mailed a letter in Canada, covering stamps, mailboxes, weight and delivery time.

title: How to Address an Envelope in Canada
abstract: A Canadian address block has no more than six lines: the addressee, the street address, then the municipality, province or territory and postal code. Postal boxes, rural routes and general delivery each have their own second line. Write the return address in the same form in the top left corner. This guide shows each format, where the postal code goes, and how window envelopes show the address.

title: Where Can You Post a Letter in Canada?
abstract: Standard letters can be posted in street mailboxes, community mailboxes and post offices, and stamps are sold at post offices and some retailers. Registered Mail cannot be dropped in a street mailbox: it must be deposited at an authorized post office. This guide explains where each kind of mail can go, how to find the nearest mailbox, and what to do if you cannot get to one.

title: Mailing Invoices and Statements in Canada Under 1,000 a Month
abstract: Canada Post's bulk letter discounts apply once you send more than 1,000 items, so a business mailing a few dozen or a few hundred statements a month pays standard Lettermail postage. The choices are to print, fold, stamp and post them yourself, to use a print-and-mail service, or to send them through an API from your billing software. This guide compares the time and cost of each at 10, 100 and 500 letters a month, and what to check before you outsource.

title: Canada Post Letter Discounts: Who Qualifies for Bulk Rates
abstract: Canada Post offers lower letter rates to businesses that send large volumes, advertised for more than 1,000 items in Canada or more than 100 internationally. Below that, businesses pay the regular Lettermail rates of $1.24 for a Permanent stamp or $1.44 for a single stamp up to 30 grams. This guide explains the threshold, what the discount applies to, and what small senders can do instead.

title: Print-and-Mail Service or Do It Yourself? A Cost Comparison
abstract: Mailing a letter yourself costs a stamp, an envelope and printing, about $1.50 to $1.75 in materials if you already own a printer, plus your time. A print-and-mail service adds a fee for printing, folding and posting. The break-even depends on volume, and at higher volumes an API with volume pricing can bring the all-in cost of a one-page letter close to the cost of the postage alone. This guide works through the numbers at one letter, ten letters and a hundred letters a month.

title: Webhooks for Physical Mail: Verifying Signatures and Handling Retries
abstract: A webhook tells your system when a letter is created, printed, mailed or cancelled. Each delivery is signed with an HMAC of the timestamp and body, so verify the signature in constant time and reject old timestamps. Answer with a 2xx within ten seconds, expect retries over about a day and a half, and handle events that arrive twice or out of order by keying on the letter id and status.

title: Send Personalised Letters From a Spreadsheet With an API
abstract: Read each row of a CSV, merge the fields into a letter template, and send up to 100 letters in one batch request. Use an idempotency key per batch so a retry cannot post a second letter, send batches one after another, and watch for per-letter errors in the response. This guide walks through a short script that mail-merges a spreadsheet into physical letters.

title: Registered Mail in Canada: What It Costs
abstract: Canada Post's price guide lists Registered Mail at $13.15 plus the applicable Lettermail postage, so a standard letter with a $1.24 stamp costs $14.39. The fee includes a signature on delivery, proof of mailing, delivery confirmation and liability coverage up to $100. It must be deposited at a post office or given to a rural carrier.

title: How Canada Post Registered Mail Works, Step by Step
abstract: You take the letter to a post office, pay the registered fee plus postage, and receive a date-stamped receipt. The recipient signs for it, a copy of the signature is available, and the delivery date is available the next business day. If it cannot be delivered it is returned when there is a return address. This guide explains each step and when it is worth the cost.

title: Sending a Written Notice by Mail in Canada: Keeping Proof
abstract: Check the contract or the rule behind your notice for how it must be given and to what address. Send it in a way that lets you show when it went and that it arrived, keep a copy of exactly what you sent, and note the date. Provincial consumer protection offices recommend proof of delivery, such as registered mail, for cancellations. This is general information and not legal advice.

title: Sending a Letter to Canada From Australia
abstract: From Australia you can post the letter yourself with Australia Post's international letter service, or order it online and have it printed and mailed inside Canada. Either way the address needs a full six-character postal code. Check Australia Post's current price and delivery time on its website, and add a return address in your own country.

title: Sending a Letter to Canada From India
abstract: From India you can post an international letter with India Post, or order a letter online to be printed and mailed within Canada as ordinary Canadian mail. A Canadian address ends in a postal code with letters and digits, not a PIN code. Check India Post's current rates, add a return address, and allow time for international transit.

title: How Long Does Registered Mail Take in Canada?
abstract: Canada Post's estimates for domestic Registered Mail are two to four business days depending on distance, and they are not guaranteed. The recipient must sign, so a missed delivery means a notice card and a pickup. This guide gives the standards and what happens when nobody is home.

title: Do Stamps Expire in Canada? Permanent Stamps and Old Stamps
abstract: A Permanent stamp is always accepted at the current domestic postage rate, even after the rate rises, so it does not expire. Older stamps with a printed value can still be used if their combined value equals or exceeds the current rate. This guide explains what to do with stamps left over from before an increase.
